text.p: Union Bank of Norway ASA, Norway's biggest savings bank, is expected to report 1996 pre-tax operating profits of 1.23 billion crowns, down from 1.41 billion crowns in 1995, according to six analysts polled by Reuters.
Two said buy, one said hold and three said sell the share, which is known as a primary capital certificate. It closed at 209.50 crowns on the Oslo Bourse on Tuesday.
The analysts said that UBN was well positioned in general in the competition in Norway's overbanked financial market.
On January 16, the bank said it would set aside 155 million crowns in the 1996 accounts to handle costs in connection with planned reductions.

UBN hopes to cut costs by an annual 200 million crowns from the year 2000 by reducing personnel and introducing new technology. The bank, which now has about 3,200 employees, plans to reduce staff by 450 people in the next few years.
UBN will present the annual result on February 13
